question: When the resistance and the capacitance of the second circuit are both on the screen, give its time constant, in seconds, and say whether it is shorter than the time constant the author gave at the start for the first circuit, with its single resistor.
question_time_note: the latest moment at which the question makes sense before its window: the second circuit is announced at 600.0-606.0 and its resistance is said and shown at 610.0-614.5; its capacitance is said and shown from 617.0

triggers.response: About 0.22 s: 4.7 kΩ × 47 µF = 0.221 s. It is not shorter: it is longer than the 0.1 s of the first circuit with its single resistor, about 2.2 times as long.
rubric: gives the time constant of the second circuit as about 0.22 s (anything from 0.21 s to 0.23 s, or the same in milliseconds)
says that it is not shorter than the time constant of the first circuit with its single resistor, 0.1 s: it is longer

beside the first circuit: 10 kΩ, 10 µF and τ = RC = 0.1 s
«The second circuit has a 4.7 kilohm resistor.»
«Its capacitor is 47 microfarads.» — said as the label appears; nothing about the capacitance comes before 617.0
the second circuit with the label 4.7 kΩ; no capacitance yet
both labels, 4.7 kΩ and 47 µF, beside the second circuit; nothing on the screen gives its time constant
both labels still beside the second circuit
«which here is about 0.15 seconds» — the author's half-voltage time for the second circuit; he never states its time constant

what the author gives away, over [617.0, 669.0]: given inside the window — none; left to the participant — items 1 and 2; given after the window — none: at 660.0-668.5 the author only asks when the second circuit reaches half its supply voltage, and his answer starts at 669.0
the reference answer is computed, not taken from the video: 4.7e3 Ω × 47e-6 F = 0.2209 s, longer than 0.1 s

validation.notes:
item 1 needs: the resistance and the capacitance shown for the second circuit
item 2 needs: the same two values and the first circuit's time constant, given at the start of the video
the when-event gives: item 1 — the capacitance of the second circuit, 47 µF, the last of the two values
